message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may hold a maximum of **one month’s rent** (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord keeps part of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc.). | • Report problems in writing (email or certified mail).
• If the landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent (after following the proper notice procedures) or repair and deduct. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are limited to **$25** per day for a single late payment, or **$50** per day for a second late payment. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan.
• Keep receipts or proof of payment. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For a month‑to‑month lease: 30‑day written notice to terminate.
• For a fixed‑term lease: you must honor the lease unless the landlord breaches. | • Provide written notice (email or certified mail). | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of entries. | | **Privacy** | • You have a right to privacy; the landlord cannot enter without notice or a valid reason. | • Report unauthorized entries to the Texas Attorney General’s Office or local housing authority. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent (after giving notice). | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Lease Termination** | • If the landlord breaches the lease (e.g., fails to maintain habitability), you may terminate the lease early. | • Provide written notice of breach and intent to terminate. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a **30‑day notice** for nonpayment or a **60‑day notice** for lease violations.
• If you fail to comply, the landlord can file an eviction lawsuit. | • Respond to the notice promptly.
• Attend the court hearing; you can present evidence of habitability or other defenses. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control; rent can increase at the end of a lease term or with a new lease. | • Review lease terms for rent increase clauses. | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify who pays utilities. | • Verify utility bills and dispute charges if necessary. | | **Insurance** | • Landlords are not required to provide renter’s insurance, but it’s highly recommended. | • Obtain a policy covering personal property and liability. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal aid for tenants (e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar associations). | • Contact a legal aid organization if you need representation. | #### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Read the lease thoroughly** – note rent amount, due date, security deposit, pet policy, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document the condition** – take photos or videos of the unit and keep a signed move‑in inspection report. 3. **Ask about utilities** – confirm which utilities you’ll pay and how they’re metered. 4. **Know your rights** – keep a copy of this summary or a link to the Texas Property Code for reference. #### When Problems Arise - **Write it down**: Keep a written record of all communications with the landlord. - **Give notice**: Provide written notice for repairs, rent disputes, or termination. - **Seek help**: If the landlord is unresponsive, contact the Texas Attorney General’s Office, the Texas Commission on Human Rights, or a local tenant advocacy group. --- **Disclaimer**: This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant rights organization.
